summary:
Our project aims to develop an interactive space simulation experience designed to introduce young people to the world of space exploration by allowing them to experience some of the challenges astronauts face during missions to the Moon and Mars.

Through different levels, players must survive for a specific number of days while completing daily missions and objectives related to space exploration, scientific research, and spacecraft or habitat maintenance.

The experience aims to demonstrate that exploring other planets is not simply about arriving, observing, and collecting information. It involves scientific responsibility, technical knowledge, and careful planning. Players will be required to collect soil and material samples, classify them, and send them to a laboratory for scientific analysis and research.

In addition, players must manage essential survival resources such as food, water, and oxygen, monitor spacecraft systems, respond to potential technical failures, and deal with environmental challenges such as radiation, dust storms, and periods of darkness when solar energy is unavailable.

Each level will introduce different conditions and challenges inspired by the real environments of the Moon and Mars. Players will need to make strategic decisions, manage limited resources, and complete their objectives to successfully survive each mission.
details:
HELIOS OUTPOST: Space Survival Simulator

What does the project do and how does it work?

HELIOS OUTPOST is an interactive educational space survival simulator designed to introduce young people to the challenges of exploring the Moon and Mars.

Players take part in simulated space missions where they must survive for a specific number of days while completing daily objectives. These missions include exploring extraterrestrial environments, collecting scientific samples, managing essential resources such as food, water, oxygen, and energy, monitoring spacecraft systems, and responding to environmental challenges such as radiation, dust storms, and periods without sunlight.

The project combines exploration, resource management, scientific research, and survival mechanics to help players understand that space exploration involves much more than simply reaching another planet.

What benefits does the project offer?

HELIOS OUTPOST provides an interactive way to learn about space exploration, planetary environments, scientific research, and the technological challenges astronauts face.

It encourages critical thinking, problem-solving, resource management, and decision-making. By completing missions and overcoming different challenges, players can develop a better understanding of the scientific and logistical requirements of future lunar and Martian exploration.

What is the expected impact of the project?

Our main goal is to make space science more accessible and engaging for young people. We want to inspire curiosity about the Moon, Mars, and future human space missions while encouraging interest in science, technology, engineering, and research.

The project aims to transform scientific information into an interactive learning experience, helping younger generations understand the importance of space exploration and the challenges humanity must overcome to explore other worlds.

What tools, programming languages, hardware, or software were used?

The project was developed using:

  • HTML: To build the structure and content of the application.
  • CSS: To design the interface and visual experience.
  • JavaScript: To implement the interactive elements and application logic.

What makes the project creative?

The creative aspect of HELIOS OUTPOST is the combination of space exploration, survival mechanics, and scientific learning in one interactive experience.

Instead of presenting space science only through text or videos, the project allows players to experience simulated mission challenges, make decisions, manage limited resources, and complete scientific objectives.

Each level introduces different environmental conditions and challenges, creating an engaging experience inspired by the realities of lunar and Martian exploration.

What factors did the team consider?

During development, we considered several important aspects:

  • Scientific accuracy and the use of NASA data sources.
  • The environmental differences between the Moon and Mars.
  • Resource management and astronaut survival requirements.
  • Space radiation and environmental hazards.
  • The importance of scientific exploration and sample collection.
  • Accessibility and ease of use for young audiences.
  • An engaging and interactive experience that combines education with entertainment.

Game Modes and Available Features

HELIOS OUTPOST offers several game modes and interactive systems designed to provide different space exploration experiences.

1. Main Menu and Game Modes

Players can access different sections of the simulator:

  • Continue: Resume an existing mission.
  • Campaign: Progress through a series of nine chapters with different challenges.
  • New Mission: Choose and start a new space exploration mission.
  • Emergency Simulation: Experience simulated cabin emergencies and learn about the challenges of maintaining a safe environment.
  • Rescue Simulation: Participate in rescue scenarios.
  • Scientific Logbook: Review scientific information and mission-related records.
  • Achievements: Track accomplishments and completed objectives.
  • How to Play: Learn the simulator's mechanics and controls.
  • Settings: Customize the experience.

2. Mission Selection and Scenarios

Players can choose from different missions with specific objectives, durations, crew sizes, cargo capacities, and difficulty levels.

Available scenarios include:

  • First Steps: An introductory training mission focused on energy management, exploration, and protection during a solar storm.
  • Shackleton Ridge: A 30-day lunar south pole mission where players must prepare their base for extended periods of darkness and solar storms.
  • April 1970: A historical scenario inspired by Apollo 13, focused on oxygen management, emergency resource conservation, and crew survival.

The simulator also includes daily challenges with unique codes, allowing players to experience the same mission conditions and compare their results. Additionally, a mission editor and teacher codes provide options for creating or accessing customized educational scenarios.

3. Resource and Life Support Management

During missions, players must continuously monitor and manage essential survival systems, including:

  • Electrical energy generation and consumption.
  • Oxygen reserves.
  • Water supplies.
  • Food supplies.
  • Cabin air conditions and carbon dioxide levels.
  • Radiation exposure.
  • Crew health and morale.
  • Scientific research progress.

These systems require players to make decisions about resource consumption, energy efficiency, and long-term mission sustainability.

4. Base Construction and Infrastructure

Players can manage and expand their lunar outpost using different infrastructure modules, including:

  • Habitats.
  • Radiation shelters.
  • Environmental Control and Life Support Systems (ECLSS).
  • Storage facilities.
  • Solar panels and batteries.
  • Fuel cells.
  • Fission reactors.
  • Greenhouses.
  • Ice extraction systems.
  • Propellant production facilities.
  • RASSOR excavators.
  • Scientific laboratories.
  • Communication antennas.
  • Service stations.

These modules represent different technologies and infrastructure concepts relevant to establishing and maintaining a sustainable human presence on the Moon.

5. Mission Control and Crew Operations

The main simulation interface provides access to several management panels:

  • Objectives: Monitor mission goals and daily tasks.
  • Modules: Manage the outpost's infrastructure.
  • Crew: Monitor crew conditions.
  • Cargo: Manage mission supplies and transported materials.
  • Logbook: Review mission records and events.

Players can also plan Extravehicular Activities (EVAs), organize exploration routes, and monitor environmental conditions such as solar illumination and available energy.

6. Multilingual Accessibility

HELIOS OUTPOST includes language options in Spanish, English, Portuguese, and French, making the simulator accessible to a wider international audience.

Through these interconnected systems, the project combines mission planning, scientific exploration, survival management, infrastructure development, and educational simulations in a single interactive experience.


7. Cargo Manifest and Mission Preparation

Before launching a mission, players select the equipment and infrastructure modules they want to transport to the lunar outpost. Each item has a specific weight and function, requiring players to manage a limited cargo capacity.

They must balance essential systems such as habitats, life support, solar panels, batteries, and storage facilities while considering the estimated autonomy of oxygen, water, and food supplies.

Once the cargo is prepared and the weight limit is respected, players can launch their mission.

This feature teaches players the importance of resource planning and logistics in space exploration, where every kilogram matters.
